# Dia-thìris – English dictionary

Here are 21313 words of the Dia-thìris tongue, in the order of their headwords; a leading article is passed over in the ordering. A noun is given with its gender, its genitive and its plural, a verb with its verbal noun, and every word with its sound between slashes. The mark ✦ follows a word that the island built from its own old roots when a new thing came to it with the humans or after them (GRAMMAR.md §13); the literal sense of such a word is set after it, as *suathaiche-nèimh* "heaven-grazer" for a tower of many floors. The other road, from English into Dia-thìris, is `LEXICON_EN.md`.


## '

- **—** det. — a (indefinite article: Dia-thìris has none; a bare noun is indefinite (cù 'a dog'); aon 'one' only when the number is meant) `F1`
- **—** det. — an (indefinite article (the form of 'a' before a vowel): Dia-thìris has none; a bare noun is indefinite (ubhal 'an apple')) `F1`
- **—** part. — of ('of' as possession or belonging: the genitive case, the possessed thing first (taigh a' bhàird 'the house of the poet', doras na h-eaglaise 'the door of the church')) `F1`

- **-idh** part. — ll ('ll: the future ending -idh/-aidh (cuiridh mi: I'll put; thig e: he'll come)) /ˈiː/ `F2`

- **-idh** part. — will (future tense: the independent future ending -idh / -aidh on the root (scrìobhaidh mi 'I will write'); the dependent form is the bare root (cha scrìobh mi)) /ˈiː/ `F1`
